subject: spec() frequency axis scaling with 'from' and 'to' args

messages.author: 7433e4ec2f9a40a6
messages.subject: spec() frequency axis scaling with 'from' and 'to' args
parts:
Hi,

I have a small question regarding the spec() function after reading the code (seewave 1.7.3). It appears that even when we supply 'from' and 'to' arguments, the x-axis is scaled as:

x <- seq(0, (f/2) - (f/wl), length.out = n%/%2)/1000

using the default window length of wl = 512 rather than, say wl = b - a. I suspect this might possibly lead to a slightly imperfect scaling. One can also supply their own wl arguments (say, wl = 2) and get clearly incorrectly scaled spectral slices.

I am also a bit unclear on the need for the (f/wl) term in the first place. Is it correcting for something in particular that I'm missing?

Thanks,
-Arvind

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] spec() frequency axis scaling with 'from' and 'to' args
parts:
Dear Arvind,

The arguments 'from' and 'to' refer to the time scale.
For instance the compute the spectrum of the first note of tico, you
should run:

data(tico)
spec(tico, from=0, to=0.5)


Now if you wish to zoom along the frequency x-axis you should use the
argument 'flim'. For instance, to zoom in between 2 and 6 kHz for the
first note:

spec(tico, from=0, to=0.5, flim=c(2,6))

Best regards,

Jerome

messages.author: 7433e4ec2f9a40a6
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] spec() frequency axis scaling with 'from' and 'to' args
parts:
Hi Jérôme,
Thanks for the prompt response.

I understand that 'from' and 'to' are used to specify a time slice of the original wave object, just as 'at=0.5' and 'wl=512' refer to a time-slice corresponding to a window of length 512 points around the specified time-point.

I assumed that the window-length argument doesn't have a meaning when the user explicitly specifies the lower and upper time bounds of the window (or at least wl should be computed rather than being specified as an argument). Yet the default value of the wl argument is still being used to compute the x-axis later on, even if it doesn't correspond to the true window length of the time slice taken.

I think the following line addition should do the right thing:
    if (!is.null(from) | !is.null(to)) {
        if (is.null(from) && !is.null(to)) {
            a <- 1
            b <- round(to * f)
        ...
            else a <- round(from * f)
            b <- round(to * f)
        }
        wl <- b - a  # set the correct window length
        wave <- as.matrix(wave[a:b, ])
    }

Thanks,
-Arvind

messages.author: acc632d9ccc1c73a
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] spec() frequency axis scaling with 'from' and 'to' args
parts:
Yes, you are absolutely right.
I will do the correction in the next version of seewave. I will just replace (b-a) by (b-a)+1.
Thanks very much for having noted this.
Jerome
